title: Cotangent obstruction and marked torsor for a small extension of the base
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C'\twoheadrightarrow C$ be a surjection of finite-dimensional commutative augmented local $k$-algebras with residue field $k$, respecting the augmentations. Write $\mathfrak m_{C'}$ for its unique maximal ideal and $I$ for its kernel, and assume $\mathfrak m_{C'}I=0$. Let $B$ be a flat $C$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], put $P=B\otimes_C k$ and $N=P\otimes_k I$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and use the full standard polynomial cotangent complex $L_{P/k}$ of [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data]. Set $T^j(P,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P)}(L_{P/k},N[j])$, with $N$ in degree zero and $D(P)$ the derived category of ordinary $P$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A marked flat lift of $B$ is a flat $C'$-algebra $B'$ with a specified $C$-algebra isomorphism $a:B'\otimes_{C'}C\cong B$; its isomorphisms must commute with $a$. There is a canonical obstruction $o(B,C'/C)\in T^2(P,N)$ which vanishes if and only if a marked flat lift exists. If it vanishes, the set of isomorphism classes of marked flat lifts is a torsor under the additive group $T^1(P,N)$: after choosing one class $x$, every other class is uniquely $x+t$. For every multiplicative subset $S\subset P$, localize $B$ and each lift at the inverse image of $S$ in the respective algebra. Under the canonical cotangent localization maps $T^j(P,N)\to T^j(S^{-1}P,S^{-1}N)$, the obstruction maps to the obstruction of the localized lifting problem, and localization of marked lifts carries $x+t$ to $x_S+t_S$. The markings and the localized isomorphisms retain the given reduction over $C$. No finite-type, isolated-singularity, or complete-intersection hypothesis on $P$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08SP, lemma-find-obstruction, with Tag 08QQ, lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex for B flat over C, and Tag 08SF, lemma-localize; flat lifts are the square-zero solutions with N=I tensor_C B, using algebra.tex Tag 051C, lemma-what-does-it-mean. Marked torsor: defos.tex lemma-choices.

proof.text: The augmentation forces $I\subset\mathfrak m_{C\prime}$, hence $I^2=0$. The $C$-action on $I$ factors through $k$ because $\mathfrak m_{C\prime}I=0$. Put $\widetilde N=I\otimes_C B$; the quotient-tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], followed by interchange of the factors, identifies it with $N=I\otimes_k P=P\otimes_k I$. Explicitly $i\otimes b\mapsto\bar b\otimes i$, with inverse $\bar b\otimes i\mapsto i\otimes b$; changing a lift of $\bar b$ adds an element of $\mathfrak m_C B$, which tensors to zero. Let $c:I\to N$ be $i\mapsto1\otimes i$.

source.place: Tag 08SP, setup of section-deformations, with algebra.tex Tag 00D2 and quotient-tensor identification.

proof.text: A marked flat lift gives a surjection $q:B\prime\to B$ using its marking. Tensor $0\to I\to C\prime\to C\to0$ with the flat $C\prime$-module $B\prime$: [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies its kernel with $I\otimes_{C\prime}B\prime$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] this is $I\otimes_C B=N$, canonically via $i\otimes b\mapsto i b\prime$ for any lift $b\prime$ of $b$. It is square zero and the structural map on $I$ is $c$. Thus it gives a square-zero solution with fixed quotient $B$ and kernel $N$. Every marking-preserving $C\prime$-isomorphism fixes this kernel identification: it sends $i b\prime$ to $i f(b\prime)$, reducing to the same $b$.

Conversely, let $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$ be a square-zero $C\prime$-algebra solution inducing $c$. Since $N=I\otimes_C B$, every $j(i\otimes b)$ equals $i e$ for any $e$ over $b$; consequently $IE=j(N)$ and $E/IE=B$. The quotient-tensor identification gives $I\otimes_{C\prime}E=I\otimes_C B=N$, and its multiplication map to $E$ is exactly $j$, hence injective. Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-ideal-flatness-criterion] to $(R,J,M)=(C\prime,I,E)$: $I^2=0$ and the quotient $B$ is flat over $C$. Thus $E$ is flat over $C\prime$. Its quotient map supplies the marking. These constructions are inverse on classes and on the allowed isomorphisms, since the kernel identification is forced by multiplication.

source.place: Tag 08SP, equation-to-solve; algebra.tex Tag 051C (lemma-what-does-it-mean), nilpotent case.

proof.text: Let $\xi=\mathrm{cl}(0\to I\to C\prime\to C\to0)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(L_{C/C\prime},I[1])$, using [lem-sfb-ring-square-zero-extension-classification] with base ring $C\prime$. Set $\eta=c_*\xi$. The same classification, with quotient map $C\to B$ and coefficient map $c$, says that square-zero solutions are exactly extension classes $z\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(L_{B/C\prime},N[1])$ whose restriction is $\eta$. Indeed the compatible map from the extension $C\prime$ to the extension $E$ must equal its given structural $C\prime$-map, because it is a map of $C\prime$-algebras. There is therefore no additional choice of a structural map or unmarked quotient hidden in this fibre.

Use the extension/restriction adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] on the one-object site, identified with ordinary modules by [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. It identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(L_{C/C\prime},N[j])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A_0,N[j])$, where $A_0=L_{C/C\prime}\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}B$. Denote again by $\eta$ the corresponding degree-one class. By [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle], the triple $C\prime\to C\to B$ gives a natural triangle $A_0\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{d}A_0[1]$, with $Y=L_{B/C\prime}$ and $Z=L_{B/C}$. Thus the map defining the fibre in Step 4 is precomposition with $u$.

source.place: Tag 08SP, displayed long exact sequence; more-algebra.tex Tag 0GMT (lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint).

proof.text: Define $o_B=\eta[1]\circ d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(Z,N[2])$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] to rotations and shifts of the triangle of Step 5. Its exactness says $o_B=0$ exactly when $\eta=z\circ u$ for some $z:Y\to N[1]$. By Steps 3--4 this is exactly existence of a marked flat lift. The triangle, $c$, and the extension class are canonical, so this defines a canonical obstruction. The same exactness says that two such $z$ differ by $t\circ v$ for a class $t:Z\to N[1]$.

source.place: Tag 08SP (lemma-find-obstruction), proof, connecting image of the base extension class.

proof.text: This $t$ is unique. To see the needed vanishing, apply [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] to the empty-variable polynomial presentation $C\prime\twoheadrightarrow C$: its naive complex is $[I/I^2\to0]$, since the universal differential of a ring over itself is zero. The full complex is nonpositive by [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data], and this comparison gives $H^0(L_{C/C\prime})=0$. Thus $L_{C/C\prime}\in D^{\leq-1}(C)$, while $N[0]\in D^{\geq0}(C)$. Orthogonality [lem-pc-derived-tstructure-orthogonality] and Step 5 give $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A_0,N)=0$. Exactness of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], after rotation, now makes $t\mapsto t\circ v$ injective. Addition $z\mapsto z+t\circ v$ consequently defines a simply transitive action on the nonempty fibre, hence on marked lifts by Steps 2--4.

source.place: Tag 08SP, torsor clause, via the class fibre; Tag 08RB, empty-variable presentation; the vanishing removes the possible kernel in the exact sequence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-flat-base-change] to the square $(C\to B)\to(k\to P)$. The required canonical map $B\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}k\to P$ is an isomorphism: $B[0]$ is a bounded-above flat resolution of itself, and [lem-trf-flat-resolution-canonical-tensor-comparison] computes this comparison by its ordinary tensor augmentation. We obtain $Z\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}P\simeq L_{P/k}$. By the adjunction of Step 5, now for $B\to P$, this yields natural group isomorphisms $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(Z,N[j])\simeq T^j(P,N)$. Define the stated obstruction and action by these isomorphisms. They involve the full cotangent complex and impose no finite-type or lci condition.

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), applied using flatness of B over C; Tag 0GMT.

proof.text: Let $T\subset B$ be the inverse image of $S$ and let $B_S=T^{-1}B$. Exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] sends a square-zero solution to an extension of $B_S$ by $N_S=S^{-1}N$. For a lift $E$, localize at the inverse image of $T$. Fractions reduce to fractions in $B_S$, and its kernel consists of the fractions with numerator in $N$: if $q(e)/q(t)=0$, multiply $e$ by a denominator so its image is zero. Kernel fractions identify with $N\otimes_B B_S$, since multiplication on $N$ factors through $B$. The reduction is canonically $B_S$, with the localized marking; multiplication still identifies the kernel with $I\otimes_C B_S$. Localization is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], so [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] makes $B_S$ flat over $C$ and every localized lift flat over $C\prime$. These statements include $0\in S$, when all the localized modules and algebras are zero.

source.place: Tag 08SF (lemma-localize); algebra.tex Tags 00CS and 00HT, applied to the exact extension and flat lifts.

proof.text: Under the natural triangle for $C\prime\to C\to B_S$, $A_0$ and $Y,Z$ map to the corresponding localized complexes. The class of the localized extension maps back to the coefficient image of its original class by [lem-sfb-ring-square-zero-extension-classification], using the actual map $E\to E_S$. Thus $\eta$ maps to $\eta_S$. Naturality of [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] gives $d_S$ as the image of $d$; hence the image of $\eta[1]d$ is $\eta_S[1]d_S$. Similarly the image of $z+t v$ is $z_S+t_S v_S$, since extension classes, cotangent maps and coefficient maps are additive and commute with composition. By [lem-trf-cotangent-augmentation-localization] the canonical cotangent maps identify localized cotangent complexes with those of $B_S/C$ and $S^{-1}P/k$. The adjunctions and square maps in Step 8 are natural, so the resulting maps on $T^j$ are exactly those obtained by localizing derived morphisms and using these cotangent identifications. Consequently $o_B\mapsto o_{B_S}$ and $x+t\mapsto x_S+t_S$. This claims natural maps, not an isomorphism from localized Ext without a finiteness hypothesis. All maps of extensions fix the reduction $B\to B_S$, so the markings and their localized isomorphisms retain the specified reduction over $C$.
